text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Talking at a pre-election rally in Osijek, President Tudjman appealed for the acceptance of Serbs who decide to choose Croatia as their homeland.
- U.N. administrator in Eastern Slavonia, Jacques Klein, announces the start of the electoral campaign in the region that is to last until April 11.
- Finance ministry conference on the new tax law proposal: A full tax system to be established by the end of 1997.
- Statistics show a two percent year-on-year rise in industrial output in February.
- The country is lacking some 3,500 teachers, while some 10,000 are currently waiting to be pensioned off.
- Croatia may soon get a commodity exchange.
- Wood trader Exportdrvo's general manager says the company is to go back to basic wood trading.
- Banking news: Hungary's Kulkereskedelmi Bank plans to buy a bank in Croatia in order to expand its business in the region.
- Croatia is to vouch for up to 50,000 kuna in individual deposits, the National Bank governor Marko Skreb says in an interview.
- Stock Exchange: Share prices mostly lower last week, only two traded shares rose. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
